title: My first job
instructions: You are going to hear five young people (A–E) talking about their first job. Match statements 1–10 with the speakers. You may choose a speaker more than once, and every speaker is the answer to at least one statement. You will hear the recording twice. There is an example (0) at the beginning.
instructionsHu: Öt fiatalt (A–E) hallasz, akik az első munkahelyükről beszélnek. Párosítsd az 1–10. állítást a beszélőkkel. Egy beszélőt többször is választhatsz, és mindegyik legalább egy állításhoz tartozik. A felvételt kétszer hallod; a 0. a példa.

script.speaker: A
script.text: My first proper job was in a little café near the cathedral. I was sixteen, and I'd never even used a coffee machine before. The first week was, honestly, a disaster. People can be really impatient when they want their coffee, and one man actually shouted at me because I'd put normal milk in his drink instead of oat milk. I went home and cried. I nearly didn't go back, but my mum talked me into it. Then, in my third week, the manager's daughter got ill, and she just handed me the keys and said, you're in charge this afternoon. I was terrified, but it went fine, and after that I felt like a completely different person. I stayed for two years in the end.

script.speaker: B
script.text: I spent the summer after my exams working in a warehouse for an online shop. I thought it'd be easy, you know, just picking things off shelves and putting them in boxes. But we were walking something like twenty kilometres a shift, and by the end of the first week my feet were in bits. The money was decent, I'll give it that, and I saved enough for a second-hand laptop. But the main thing was, I spent hours every day with nothing to think about except what I wanted to do with my life. By September I'd decided to apply for engineering, which I'd never seriously considered before. So in a strange way, that boring job was the best career advice I ever got.

script.speaker: C
script.text: I did a three-month internship at a marketing agency in Chicago. It sounds glamorous, but it was unpaid. They gave us lunch vouchers and covered our travel, and that was it. A lot of the time I was doing exactly the same work as the paid junior staff, which, looking back, really wasn't fair. My aunt said I should complain, but I didn't want to cause trouble. Anyway, I kept in touch with one of the designers there, and about six months later she moved to another company and recommended me for a junior position. So now I'm actually earning money in the industry. I'm still not a fan of unpaid internships, though. Not everyone can afford to work for nothing.

script.speaker: D
script.text: My first job was as a lifeguard at the local swimming pool, and I have to be honest, my uncle was the manager, so I didn't exactly have to compete for it. That actually made things harder, though. I could tell some of the others thought I hadn't earned my place, so I always arrived early, and I volunteered for the worst shifts – Sunday mornings, cleaning the changing rooms, you name it. The scariest moment was when I was checking my phone for, like, ten seconds, and when I looked up, a little boy had slipped under the water in the deep end. I got to him straight away and he was fine, but I've never looked at my phone on duty since.

script.speaker: E
script.text: I worked on the checkouts at a big supermarket on Saturdays during my last year of school. I'd expected to be surrounded by other students, but most of my colleagues were women in their fifties and sixties, and they were brilliant – funny, kind, and they'd seen everything. One of them, Pat, taught me more about handling money than any lesson at school. The problem was the new manager. He kept changing my shifts at the last minute, even when I'd told him I had exams, and in the end we had a big argument. I was supposed to stay until the summer, but I handed in my notice in March. I don't regret it, but I do miss Pat.

example.prompt: This person got the job through a relative.
example.explanation: D (Jack) a helyes: a nagybátyja volt az uszoda vezetője, így nem kellett versenyeznie az állásért.
example.evidence: my uncle was the manager, so I didn't exactly have to compete for it

items.prompt: This person received no wages for the work.
items.explanation: C (Aisha) a helyes: a gyakornoki munkája fizetés nélküli volt („it was unpaid”) – csak ebédjegyet és útiköltséget kapott.
items.evidence: It sounds glamorous, but it was unpaid.

wrongOptions.D: Jack „volunteered for the worst shifts” – ez azt jelenti, hogy önként vállalta a legrosszabb műszakokat, nem azt, hogy nem kapott fizetést.

items.prompt: This person found it hard to cope with demanding customers at first.
items.explanation: A (Chloe) a helyes: az első hét katasztrófa volt, a vendégek türelmetlenek voltak, egy férfi még rá is kiabált a rossz tej miatt, és ő sírva ment haza.
items.evidence: one man actually shouted at me because I'd put normal milk in his drink instead of oat milk

wrongOptions.E: Sophie a pénztárnál dolgozott, de nála nem a vásárlókkal, hanem az új vezetővel volt gond.

items.prompt: This person got on particularly well with much older colleagues.
items.explanation: E (Sophie) a helyes: diáktársakra számított, de a kollégái többsége ötvenes-hatvanas éveiben járó nő volt, akiket nagyszerűnek tartott; egyikük, Pat, sokat tanított neki.
items.evidence: most of my colleagues were women in their fifties and sixties, and they were brilliant

wrongOptions.C: Aisha egy tervezővel tartotta a kapcsolatot, de nem mondja, hogy idősebb kollégákkal jött ki különösen jól.

items.prompt: This person was surprised by how physically tiring the job was.
items.explanation: B (Liam) a helyes: azt hitte, könnyű lesz, de műszakonként kb. húsz kilométert gyalogoltak, és egy hét után teljesen tönkrement a lába („my feet were in bits”).
items.evidence: we were walking something like twenty kilometres a shift

wrongOptions.D: Jack takarította az öltözőt, de nem mondja, hogy a munka fizikailag meglepően fárasztó lett volna.

items.prompt: This person felt they had to prove themselves because of how they got the job.
items.explanation: D (Jack) a helyes: érezte, hogy a többiek szerint nem érdemelte ki a helyét (a nagybátyja révén kapta meg), ezért mindig korán érkezett, és önként vállalta a legrosszabb műszakokat.
items.evidence: I could tell some of the others thought I hadn't earned my place, so I always arrived early

wrongOptions.C: Aisha nagynénje csak azt tanácsolta, hogy panaszkodjon – nem rajta keresztül kapta az állást.

items.prompt: A contact this person made later led to a paid position.
items.explanation: C (Aisha) a helyes: tartotta a kapcsolatot az egyik tervezővel, aki hat hónappal később egy másik cégnél beajánlotta őt egy junior állásra – most már fizetést kap.
items.evidence: she moved to another company and recommended me for a junior position

wrongOptions.D: Jack a nagybátyja révén kapta az első munkáját, nem egy később szerzett kapcsolat révén jutott fizetett álláshoz.

items.prompt: This person left the job earlier than planned.
items.explanation: E (Sophie) a helyes: nyárig kellett volna maradnia, de egy nagy veszekedés után a vezetővel már márciusban felmondott.
items.evidence: I was supposed to stay until the summer, but I handed in my notice in March

wrongOptions.A: Chloe majdnem nem ment vissza az első hét után, de végül két évig maradt.

items.prompt: This person was put in charge sooner than they expected.
items.explanation: A (Chloe) a helyes: már a harmadik héten a kezébe nyomták a kulcsokat azzal, hogy aznap délután ő a felelős – meg is rémült, tehát erre nem számított.
items.evidence: she just handed me the keys and said, you're in charge this afternoon

wrongOptions.D: Jack vízimentőként felelt a gyerekekért, de nem mondja, hogy váratlanul vezető szerepet kapott volna.

items.prompt: This person describes a moment of carelessness that could have ended badly.
items.explanation: D (Jack) a helyes: tíz másodpercre a telefonját nézte, és közben egy kisfiú a víz alá csúszott a mély részen; szerencsére azonnal kimentette.
items.evidence: I was checking my phone for, like, ten seconds

wrongOptions.A: Chloe tévedett a tejjel, de ennek nem lehettek komoly következményei – csak a vendég kiabált.

items.prompt: The job helped this person decide what to study.
items.explanation: B (Liam) a helyes: az unalmas munka közben sokat gondolkodott a jövőjén, és szeptemberre eldöntötte, hogy mérnöknek jelentkezik – ezt nevezi a legjobb pályatanácsnak.
items.evidence: By September I'd decided to apply for engineering

wrongOptions.C: Aisha már a szakmájában dolgozik, de nála a munka nem a továbbtanulásról szóló döntést segítette.
